text:
marta: Quick sync — I'm starting checkpoint conversion for nova-35b. Raw weights are in s3://redwood-models/onboard/nova-35b/raw-v1. Target: safetensors, fp16, 8 shards for TP=8, and a HuggingFace-style config. Two potential quirks I know about: tokenizer uses sentencepiece and there is a tokenizer.json alongside the .spm, and some TP layouts we've seen use tp_first vs tp_last ordering. Anyone already converted this or seen odd tokenization/axis ordering?

ashwin: I ran a dry run yesterday. Short notes: use safetensors to avoid pickle issues, run the tp-reshape step (reshape kernels expect a specific axis ordering), and double-check bias split pattern — some checkpoints split biases by TP dim. Pushed a helper script to infra/onboard-scripts. Link: https://git.redwood/infralab/onboard-scripts/tree/main/convert_nova35b 

ashwin: copy of the command I used:
```bash
python convert_checkpoint.py \
  --input s3://redwood-models/onboard/nova-35b/raw-v1/pytorch_model.bin \
  --output s3://redwood-models/onboard/nova-35b/safetensors/v1/ \
  --dtype fp16 \
  --shards 8 \
  --tp-layout tp_last \
  --check-bias-split \
```

ashwin: and a minimal config we drop into HF format (quick example):
```json
{
  "model_type": "causal",
  "hidden_size": "4096",
  "num_attention_heads": "32",
  "tensor_parallel": 8,
  "dtype": "fp16",
  "tokenizer": "sentencepiece"
}
```

samir: Heads-up on tokenizer: the .spm file uses a legacy unk id 0 while our HF pipeline expects unk=3. I handled this before by running the spm export with a remap step. Quick one-liner to remap ids in tokenizer.json: `python tools/spm_remap.py --input tokenizer.json --map 0:3 --output tokenizer.remap.json` — then generate tokenizer files from that before packaging. :eyes:

toni: For serving layout, prefer packing 4 shards per host (so 2 hosts for TP=8) and let the runtime do TP stripe across hosts. Add runtime hint `tp_split: host_stripe` in the model manifest so router/runtime picks the right kernel. Also add `kv_cache_bytes_per_token` estimate to manifest to avoid OOMs on long-context runs.

ashwin: small gotcha: if you convert to bf16 accidentally (we had one CI job do this), the GPU kernel path differs and perf regresses. Make sure `--dtype fp16` explicit. Also check that all layernorm params remain fp32 if you're using fused kernels (some ops expect fp32 epsilon).

infra-bot: CI job scheduled: onboard-convert-nova35b #1245. Artifacts will land at gs://redwood-onboard/nova-35b/1245/ and a presigned s3 mirror will appear. Logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/1245 :gear:

ashwin: While testing generations, validate with these quick checks: 1) short prompt ("Hello") -> deterministic shape; 2) kv cache step run two-step and verify identical tokens; 3) sample with temp=0.0 and check no NaNs. If bias split wrong you'll see tiny numeric drift but consistent shape mismatch.

marta: Perfect — I'll kick the conversion with ashwin's flags now and watch job 1245. I'll open a PR `refs/heads/onboard/nova35b-conv` with the manifest and tokenizer remap notes. Can folks review once CI artifacts are up? :thumbsup:

toni: Happy to review manifest. Quick checklist I usually run: model sharding map, tp_layout annotation, kv_cache estimate, tokenizer files present (.spm + tokenizer.json or tokenizer.remap.json), and a tiny runbook snippet for local smoke test.

samir: If anyone hits sentencepiece normalization differences, ping me — I have the remap table we used for other onboards.

marta: Thanks — will ping when PR is up. If CI passes I'll tag for internal canary. :rocket:
